# Issue 2: Splitting a damage charge two ways loses a cent

## Outcome

Every penny of a damage charge is billed to someone. The shares from `splitCharge` add up to the
charge. Charge D-301 (3333 cents) split two ways gives 1667 and 1666 cents, not 1666 and 1666.

## Requirements

- When a charge does not divide evenly by the number of borrowers, the system shall give each borrower the rounded-down share and hand out the leftover cents one each, starting with the first borrower.
- The system shall return shares that add up to exactly the charge, for every charge and number of borrowers.
- The system shall return shares that differ from each other by at most one cent.
- When a charge divides evenly, the system shall give every borrower the same share.

## Must not change

- Amounts stay integer cents. No floats.
- `splitCharge(totalCents, ways)` keeps its name, arguments and return type (`number[]` of length `ways`).
- A negative or non-integer charge, or fewer than one borrower, is still refused with an error.
- Nothing under `src/auth/` changes.
- The existing tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` stay as they are.

## Out of scope

- Late fees (`src/fees/late.ts`).
- Weighted or unequal splits.
- Changes to how `bun run desk split` prints amounts.

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/fees/split.test.ts` pass, and so do the existing ones.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.

The spec is written and the new tests fail on the current code, as they should. Nothing under `src/` was changed.

I didn't have the triage output, so I assumed it named `src/fees/split.ts` and `tests/fees/split.test.ts`. Those are the only files I read.

- **Spec:** `specs/2/SPEC.md` has the five sections. It has four "The system shall"/"When" requirements: the leftover cents are handed out one each starting with the first borrower, the shares add up to the charge, the shares differ by at most one cent, and an even charge gives equal shares. Splitting D-301 (3333 cents) two ways should give 1667 and 1666.
- **Tests:** I added four tests to `tests/fees/split.test.ts`, one per requirement. The existing three are unchanged.
- **Run:** `bun test tests` gives 12 pass and 2 fail. The two failures are the leftover-cents test (it gets `[1666, 1666]` instead of `[1667, 1666]`) and the sum test (a 1-cent charge split two ways totals 0). The other two new tests pass on the current code. Even splits and a one-cent spread already hold, so they only guard against regressions.
